── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 27, 37, 53, 40 mi
This week: 42 mi over 5 runs.
Feeling: "Anxious about the new date."
Asks: "The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: With the race now 2 weeks out, skip the 22-miler and treat this as your last real work week before taper. …
Answers: (1) No, do not add a 22-miler now. … (2) Here is what matters more than mileage: you have a 20 and a 17 in the last 4 weeks, both finished strong and even-paced, and your easy pace at 139 bpm is steady. That is a body that is ready.
Next week:
Mon: rest. Full day off to recover from Sunday's 17.
Tue: easy, 6 mi, heart rate under 145. Shake out the long run, nothing more.
Wed: quality, 9 mi with 2 mi warm-up, 5 mi at marathon pace around 8:35/mi, 2 mi…
Thu: easy, 5 mi, heart rate under 145. Recovery from the marathon-pace work.
Fri: rest. Full day off before the weekend.
Sat: easy, 4 mi, with 4 x 20 sec strides at the end. Keeps the legs sharp before Sunday.
Sun: long, 16 mi, first 12 easy around 9:55/mi, last 4 at marathon pace around 8:35/mi…
